persona: Relaxed, types fast on the phone and does not fix typos. Says the heat pump was put in back in March 2024; has one photo, the installer's invoice and a repair quote.
initial_message: hi so on sunday 13th my box trailer rolled back down the driveway and smashed into the heat pump outside unit on the side of our house. the unit is totaly crushed and a couple of weatherboards behind it are cracked. noone was hurt. how do i claim on my house insurence

facts.incident.description: I had unhitched our box trailer at the top of the sloping driveway and put a brick behind the wheel. The brick slipped and the trailer rolled back about five metres into the side of the house, straight into the heat pump outdoor unit.
facts.incident.cause: The unhitched box trailer rolled back down the sloping driveway into the house
facts.loss.description: Heat pump outdoor unit crushed: casing caved in, fan guard bent, and the heat pump no longer works. Two weatherboards behind the unit are cracked.
property.affected_areas: heat pump outdoor unit on the side wall
facts.mitigation.emergency_action: Switched the heat pump off at its outdoor isolation switch and at the switchboard, and pulled the trailer away
facts.policyholder.name: Emily Tarataholm
facts.heat_pump.description: Aerowai 5.0 kW high-wall heat pump, indoor and outdoor unit
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the crushed outdoor unit and the cracked weatherboards, taken the same afternoon. Available now.
facts.evidence.receipt: The invoice for the heat pump from Ash Tarn Electrical, who supplied and installed it. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Nikau Ridge Sparks dated 16 September 2026, total $4,283.75 including GST. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_invoice_date: the heat pump went in back in march 2024. i dont know why the invoice says september
facts.if_asked_about_indoor_unit: The indoor unit on the lounge wall was not damaged.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo, close-up of a plain white heat pump outdoor unit standing on a small concrete pad against pale grey painted weatherboards on the side of a house. The top and front of the white metal casing are caved in and crumpled, the round black fan grille on the front is bent inward, and a corner of the casing is split open. The two weatherboards directly behind the unit are cracked and split along the grain where they show above its top edge. Concrete driveway in the foreground, late afternoon sunlight. The frame shows only the crushed unit, its copper pipes and the wall around it; the casing is plain and unmarked.
materials.purpose: Shows the crushed heat pump outdoor unit and the cracked weatherboards

design.notes: Planted feature ownership_doc_after_loss: the heat pump invoice prints a purchase date of 21 September 2026, eight days after the trailer hit the unit on 13 September 2026, while the claimant says it was installed in March 2024. The repair quote (16 September 2026) is after the incident, so only the ownership check fires.

triage.rationale: The heat pump invoice (serial AW50-TST-2023) prints a purchase date of 21 September 2026, after the incident on 13 September 2026. That is a strong indicator, so a person must look, and it is a material that contradicts the claimant's statement that the heat pump was installed in March 2024. Allowed but not required: the claimant answers "i dont know why" when asked about the invoice date (question_unanswered). Nothing else applies: nobody is hurt, no other party, the home is habitable, the photo and a complete quote (NZD 4,283.75 including GST, under 5,000) are supplied. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Invoice purchase date 21 September 2026 is after the last possible incident day, 13 September 2026

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 April 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2019-04-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
